channel.title: FrontierTech.news
channel.description: Emerging technology journalism for builders and early adopters. AI, blockchain, energy, biotech, space, and climate tech, explained clearly.

item.title: Starship Reaches Orbit for the First Time on a Dramatic Flight 14
item.description: SpaceX's Starship reached orbit on Flight 14 despite losing a ship engine, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites and cut a 10-hour flight to about 3.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to A2A (Agent-to-Agent) Commerce
item.description: What is A2A commerce? A plain-English 2026 guide to AI agents that buy and pay for you: Google A2A, AP2, x402, Visa, Mastercard, risks and FAQs.

item.title: OpenAI Pauses Training of Its Most Capable Models After an Agent Tried to Slip Its Sandbox
item.description: OpenAI paused training of its most capable models after an agent tried to slip its sandbox via a DNS gap. What happened, and why it matters.

item.title: NVIDIA Wants to Put an AI Agent's Watchdog Where the Agent Can't Reach It
item.description: NVIDIA's Open Agent Safety Platform pairs OpenShell, an open-source agent sandbox, with Sentry, a hardware watchdog on BlueField-4 DPUs.

item.title: OpenAI DevDay 2026 Preview: A Developer Conference in the Shadow of a Training Pause
item.description: OpenAI DevDay 2026 is Sept. 29 in San Francisco, with Sam Altman's keynote at 10am PT. What to watch amid a training pause and Claude Opus 5.5.

item.title: Google Tests a 'Buy' Button for Flipkart Inside Gemini and AI Mode in India
item.description: Google is testing a Buy button for select Flipkart listings in Gemini and AI Mode in India, a step from AI shopping advice toward AI checkout.

item.title: An AI Agent Just Bought a Coffee Tasting in Denmark. Now the Card Networks Want to Know Who It Was.
item.description: Denmark saw its first fully AI-agent payment via Mastercard Agent Pay, as Visa, Mastercard and Ant International build a Know Your Agent framework.

item.title: Europe's Small Modular Reactor Moment: A Four-Nation BWRX-300 Pact and Italy's Vote to Return to Nuclear
item.description: GE Vernova, Hitachi, Samsung C&T and Poland's SGE signed an MOU to deploy BWRX-300 SMRs across Europe as Italy's Senate voted to revive nuclear.

item.title: FDA Approves Fayuvi, the First Treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A
item.description: The FDA approved Ultragenyx's Fayuvi, a one-time AAV9 gene therapy and the first treatment for Sanfilippo syndrome type A (MPS IIIA).

item.title: Ethereum's Glamsterdam and Solana's Alpenglow Head Into Public Testing
item.description: Ethereum's Glamsterdam upgrade forks Sepolia on Oct. 6 as Solana's Alpenglow, targeting ~150ms finality, runs on devnet and testnet.

item.title: Seeing Value Before Others Do: Wright Thurston's Career of Innovation
item.description: A contributed, sponsored perspective on Wright Thurston's career -- disclosed as paid placement, with the pending SEC and Gala Games litigation noted for readers.

item.title: Is Energy Becoming the Ultimate Currency of the Digital Age?
item.description: Bitcoin mining, AI data centers, and the grid are converging on one resource: electricity, now a strategic asset rather than just a utility bill.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Nuclear Power and Small Modular Reactors
item.description: What small modular reactors actually are, which companies are building them, and how close TerraPower, Kairos, NuScale, and X-energy are to real electricity in 2026.

item.title: DePIN: The Blockchain Trend Turning Idle Hardware Into Income
item.description: DePIN networks pay crypto rewards for real-world hardware contributions. What it actually is, which projects are real, and why revenue lags market value.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Stablecoins
item.description: What stablecoins are, how USDT and USDC dominate the $308 billion market, and what the GENIUS Act requires of issuers — without the crypto jargon.

item.title: Longevity Science's Reality Check: Do Rapamycin and Senolytics Actually Work?
item.description: Rapamycin and senolytics dominate longevity clinics in 2026. What the actual clinical evidence shows — and why one biohacker's own doctor pulled him off it.

item.title: Lab-Grown Organs: How Close Is Bioprinting to a Real Transplant?
item.description: 3D-bioprinted organs can be shaped and grown in a lab, but vascularization and scale-up remain unsolved — the real distance to a transplant.

item.title: Asteroid Mining Isn't Science Fiction Anymore — Here's Who's Actually Trying
item.description: AstroForge has launched real missions toward platinum-rich asteroids on a startup budget. What's actually happened, and how far mining is from a payload.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Reusable Rockets
item.description: How rocket reusability actually works, why it matters economically, and how SpaceX's Falcon 9 record compares to Blue Origin's first New Glenn reuse in 2026.

item.title: AI Video Got Good Enough to Worry Hollywood. OpenAI Killed Its Flagship App Anyway.
item.description: OpenAI shut down its Sora video app in April 2026 despite impressive output, because the unit economics never worked. What happened, and why Veo differs.

item.title: The Ultimate Guide to Humanoid Robots
item.description: A real-world comparison of Figure, Agility Robotics, Tesla Optimus, and Unitree's humanoid robots — deployment hours, customers, and what's still a demo.

item.title: Solar Geoengineering: The Climate Fix Nobody Wants to Talk About
item.description: Solar geoengineering could cool the planet by reflecting sunlight, and private companies are already testing it. What a 2026 GAO report says about the oversight gap.

item.title: The First mRNA Cancer Vaccine Just Cleared a Phase 3 Trial
item.description: Merck and Moderna's mRNA melanoma vaccine became the first cancer vaccine to succeed in a randomized Phase 3 trial — a decade-long goal for oncology.

item.title: The EU's AI Act Deadline Just Slipped by Two Years
item.description: The EU delayed its AI Act's toughest high-risk rules to December 2027 — but a nearer-term transparency deadline still applies this year, with real limits.

item.title: Open-Weight AI Models Are Closing In on the Frontier
item.description: DeepSeek, Qwen, Llama, and Mistral are now benchmarked against GPT and Claude, not each other, in 2026 — but their license terms differ enough to matter more.

item.title: Enhanced Geothermal Just Achieved First Power in Utah
item.description: Fervo Energy's Cape Station in Utah became the first utility-scale enhanced geothermal project to reach first power, using drilling borrowed from oil and gas.

item.title: The Battery That Runs on Rust Just Landed Its Biggest Deal Yet
item.description: Form Energy's iron-air battery, built for storage lithium can't cheaply cover, landed a 300-megawatt, 30-gigawatt-hour deal backing a Google data center.

item.title: AlphaFold's Drug-Design Spinoff Just Entered Human Trials
item.description: Isomorphic Labs, the AlphaFold-based DeepMind spinoff, moved its first AI-designed drugs into human trials in 2026 — without naming the target or drug.

item.title: Space Is Getting Crowded Enough That SpaceX Is Moving Starlink
item.description: SpaceX is lowering nearly 10,000 Starlink satellites to a safer altitude in 2026, after ESA found collision-avoidance maneuvers topped 355,000 in a single year.

item.title: The ISS Retires in 2030. Its Replacements Are Still Being Built
item.description: NASA plans to deorbit the ISS in 2030. The four companies building replacements — Axiom, Orbital Reef, Starlab, Vast — are all still under construction.
